items.title: Pay invoice for wedding invitations
items.quote: Den Rechnungsbetrag überweisen Sie bitte binnen 14 Tagen nach dem Rechnungsdatum.
items.computation: The invoice is dated 26.01.2026 (Monday). Under §187 BGB the 14-day period begins the day after the triggering event, so it starts on 27.01.2026 and its 14th day falls on 09.02.2026 (Monday), which is not a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in NW, so no §193 BGB extension applies. However, the letter also prints an explicit due date 'Zahlbar bis: 16.02.2026', which is a week later and contradicts the 14-day calculation from the invoice date. Following the rule to use the earliest plausible date when a letter contradicts itself, 09.02.2026 is used, with reduced confidence and a warning about the discrepancy.

warnings: The letter gives two conflicting due dates: '14 Tagen nach dem Rechnungsdatum' (which computes to 09.02.2026) versus the explicitly printed 'Zahlbar bis: 16.02.2026' — the earlier date (09.02.2026) was used to be safe, but the recipient should double-check with the sender which date actually applies.
